net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
Investment advisory and administration fees increased from the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher average assets under management.

Total investment advisory and administration fees from wealth vehicles compared with average assets under management implied an annualized effective fee rate of 66.9 bps and 67.5 bps for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Total investment advisory fees from institutional accounts compared with average assets under management implied an annualized effective fee rate of 37.4 bps and 38.2 bps for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in the implied annualized effective fee rate is primarily due to a shift in the mix of assets under management.

Total investment advisory and administration fees from closed-end funds compared with average assets under management implied an annualized effective fee rate of 89.3 bps and 89.2 bps for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Distribution and service fees increased from the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to higher average assets under management in mutual funds, partially offset by a shift into lower fee paying share classes.

Institutional.heading: Institutional
Institutional.text:
Assets under management in institutional accounts at September 30, 2026 increased 4.3% to $36.2 billion from $34.7 billion at September 30, 2025. Activity during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included:

• Net outflows of $167 million including $384 million from real estate, partially offset by net inflows of $250 million into global listed infrastructure;

• Market appreciation of $1.8 billion including $1.4 billion from real estate; and

• Distributions of $450 million from real estate.

Closed-end funds.heading: Closed-end funds
Closed-end funds.text:
Assets under management in closed-end funds at September 30, 2026 increased 2.3% to $12.0 billion from $11.8 billion at September 30, 2025. Activity during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 included:

• Net inflows of $206 million primarily from real estate;

• Market appreciation of $283 million including $149 million from real estate and $131 million from global listed infrastructure; and

• Distributions of $505 million including $171 million from real estate, $163 million from global listed infrastructure and $149 million from preferred securities.

intro.text: Cohen & Steers, founded in 1986, is a global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternative income, including listed and private real estate, preferred securities, infrastructure, resource equities, commodities, as well as multi-strategy solutions. Headquartered in New York City, with offices in London, Dublin, Hong Kong, Tokyo and Singapore, we serve institutional and individual investors around the world. Cohen & Steers, Inc. (CNS) was organized as a Delaware corporation on March 17, 2004. CNS is the holding company for its direct and indirect subsidiaries, including Cohen & Steers Capital Management, Inc. (CSCM), Cohen & Steers Securities, LLC (CSS), Cohen & Steers UK Limited (CSUK), Cohen & Steers Ireland Limited (CSIL), Cohen & Steers Asia Limited (CSAL), Cohen & Steers Japan Limited (CSJL) and Cohen & Steers Singapore Private Limited (CSSG).

Institutional accounts.heading: Institutional accounts
Institutional accounts.text:

• Net outflows of $324 million including $316 million from real assets multi-strategy (included in "Other"); and

• Market appreciation of $1.8 billion including $702 million from global/international real estate, $522 million from global listed infrastructure and $310 million from U.S. real estate.

• Market appreciation of $1.0 billion including $458 million from global/international real estate, $286 million from global listed infrastructure and $269 million from U.S. real estate; and

• Distributions of $667 million including $638 million from U.S. real estate.

Closed-end funds.heading: Closed-end funds
Closed-end funds.text:

• Net inflows of $621 million including $513 million attributable to the Cohen & Steers Infrastructure Fund, Inc. (UTF) rights offering, including leverage;

• Market appreciation of $775 million including $383 million from global listed infrastructure and $227 million from preferred securities; and

• Distributions of $638 million including $227 million from U.S. real estate and $199 million from preferred securities.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: As of December 31, 2025, our largest institutional client, Daiwa Asset Management, which held most of its assets in U.S. real estate strategies subadvised by us in Japan, represented approximately 4.5% of total revenue and approximately 8.7% of our total assets under management for 2025.
Performance, price and brand are our principal sources of competition.
Returns on investments in real estate securities depend on the amount of income and capital appreciation or loss realized by the underlying real property.
